reason: The pointwise limit is identified explicitly, and the negation of uniform convergence is verified with a fixed positive epsilon.
text:
For each \(x\in[0,1)\), \(x^n\to0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
Any uniform limit would necessarily equal this pointwise limit. Fix \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12\). For every \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), take \(n=N\) and \(x=2^{-1/N}<1\). Then
\[
|f_n(x)-f(x)|=x^n=\left(2^{-1/N}\right)^N=\tfrac12.
\]
Hence for every \(N\) there exist \(n\ge N\) and \(x\in[0,1]\) such that \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\). Therefore \((f_n)\) does not converge uniformly on \([0,1]\).
